original_question: Which polynomials on C^2 are projectively isotrivial, in the sense that their generic fibers all have isomorphic smooth projective models?
target_in_paper: M. Zaidenberg, §2 "Exotic C^n's", item 2.2, specifically the follow-up question: "By the way, is it possible to describe those polynomials ... which are projectively isotrivial in the sense that their generic fibres all have isomorphic smooth projective models?"
correct_elements: Your draft captures the right secondary question in the paper and uses essentially the paper’s own defining phrase for "projectively isotrivial": the generic fibers have isomorphic smooth projective models. It also correctly keeps the problem in the plane-polynomial setting suggested by the nearby two-variable context (Kaliman’s problem and Russell’s field generators).
missing_details: Make explicit that the object is a polynomial map f in C[x,y], i.e. a regular function f: C^2 -> C.

Replace the informal phrase "generic fibers" with a precise quantifier, e.g. there exists a nonempty Zariski-open subset U of C such that for all t in U the fibers f^{-1}(t) are the ones being compared.
Clarify that one compares the smooth projective models (equivalently, smooth projective completions/models) of the general affine fibers f^{-1}(t), not necessarily the affine fibers themselves.
State the task as "describe" or "characterize" this class of polynomials; the paper does not, at this point, restate a specific equivalence relation for classification in §2.2.

Indicate the nearby paper context: this is a side question attached to Zaidenberg’s item 2.2, not the main 2.2 question about whether a polynomial defining a contractible hypersurface must already be isotrivial in the ordinary sense.

If one wants the surrounding paper-faithful context included, note that the paper immediately remarks that all generically rational polynomials, i.e. field generators in Russell’s sense, belong to this class.
refined_question: Describe the complex plane polynomials f in C[x,y] such that there exists a nonempty Zariski-open subset U of C with the property that, for every t in U, the affine curve f^{-1}(t) has a smooth projective model independent of t up to isomorphism; equivalently, for general t1,t2 in C, the smooth projective models of f^{-1}(t1) and f^{-1}(t2) are isomorphic.
justification: The draft is not aiming at Zaidenberg’s main §2.2 question about contractible hypersurfaces implying ordinary isotriviality; rather, it matches the immediately following side-question that asks to describe polynomials that are "projectively isotrivial" and then defines that phrase exactly by requiring the generic fibres to have isomorphic smooth projective models. The nearby Kaliman discussion supplies the comparison notion "isotrivial" as "generic fibers are pairwise isomorphic," and Russell’s Question 3 is cited there to identify generically rational polynomials with field generators, which the paper notes are examples in the projectively isotrivial class. Because that local context is explicitly about polynomials in two variables, keeping the refined question on C^2 stays narrow and faithful to the paper’s intent rather than broadening it to higher-dimensional hypersurface problems.
